column2: A magistrate in the river district has been selling favorable judgments. A farmer's widow says her neighbor's field was awarded to a merchant who paid in silver, and that the magistrate's clerk keeps a second ledger. The magistrate is a cousin of the district's richest landholder, and the district has been quiet for years.
Remove the magistrate and try him before your court.
Fine him and leave him in office.
Send him to a distant post and warn his family.

The harvest rolls are short by a tenth. Your steward swears the measure is honest. The village elders say the new collector's scoop is wider than the old one. The granary is half full, and the winter is long. The levy is due in six weeks.
Open the granary and forgive the shortfall.
Enforce the levy and use the collector's measure.
Send your own clerk to re-measure the harvest.

The village below the pass wants a stone wall before the next raiding season. The local earthbenders can raise it in a month, but they ask for a share of the village's fields and the right to keep their own officers. The headman says the wall is worth any price. The elders say the earthbenders will become the new landlords.
Grant the earthbenders their fields and officers.
Levy the earthbenders and pay them in grain.
Refuse the wall and move the village to the pass fort.

A column of refugees from the war in the eastern provinces has reached your border. They have carts, goats, and too many children. The garrison says they will eat the winter stores. The village elders say the Earth Kingdom cannot turn its own people away. The column's headman asks for fallow fields and your protection.
Settle them on the fallow fields and share the stores.
Close the border and send them east.
Take the able-bodied into the levy and send the rest on.

A trade caravan bound for the Si Wong oasis towns needs a guide. The sandbenders know the dunes, but their chief demands a toll in water and a promise that no earthbender will follow the caravan's track. Your caravan master says the sandbenders will lead the goods into a trap.
Hire the sandbenders and pay their toll.
Send your own guide and bar the sandbenders from the route.
Cancel the caravan and wait for the next caravan season.

A company of Kyoshi Warriors has come to your court. Their captain says the eastern coast is open to raiders, and that her women can train your guards in the fan and the blade. The garrison captain does not want island women teaching his men. The village elders remember that the Kyoshi Warriors have kept their island free for generations.
Take the Kyoshi Warriors as instructors.
Take them into your service and send them to the coast.
Politely refuse and strengthen the local levy.
